q: The burning wood in the air releases heat and ____ energies.
e: The burning wood in the air releases heat and light energies. Burning wood gives out heat and light as chemical energy is released.

q: Photosynthesis is the chemical reaction that occurs when plants use energy from the sun, carbon dioxide, and water to synthesise the ____ that the plant needs to survive.
e: Photosynthesis is the chemical reaction that occurs when plants use energy from the sun, carbon dioxide, and water to synthesise the food that the plant needs to survive. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: Whenever a chemical reaction (chemical change) occurs, energy is usually transferred to or from the ____.
e: Whenever a chemical reaction (chemical change) occurs, energy is usually transferred to or from the surroundings. The surroundings are everything outside the reaction you chose to study.

q: Changing states of matter (physical change) also involve ____ changes.
e: Changing states of matter (physical change) also involve energy changes. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: There are various kinds of energy such as kinetic energy (due to the movement), potential energy (due to the position), electrical energy, light energy, thermal energy, chemical energy, ____ energy, etc.
e: There are various kinds of energy such as kinetic energy (due to the movement), potential energy (due to the position), electrical energy, light energy, thermal energy, chemical energy, mechanical energy, etc. Mechanical is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In addition, energy can neither be created nor destroyed as stated in the Law of Conservation of ____.
e: In addition, energy can neither be created nor destroyed as stated in the Law of Conservation of Energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: However, energy can change from one form to another without a net loss or gain of energy and it is called energy ____.
e: However, energy can change from one form to another without a net loss or gain of energy and it is called energy transformation. Transformation is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: electric motor (electrical energy into ____ energy)
e: Electric motor (electrical energy into kinetic energy). Kinetic is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: hair dryer (electrical energy into ____ energy)
e: Hair dryer (electrical energy into thermal energy). Thermal is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: battery (chemical energy into ____ energy)
e: Battery (chemical energy into electrical energy). Electrical is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: automobile engine (chemical energy into ____ energy)
e: Automobile engine (chemical energy into mechanical energy). Mechanical is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: solar cell (light energy into ____ energy)
e: Solar cell (light energy into electrical energy). Electrical is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Chemical energy is the energy that is stored in the ____ of chemical compounds such as atoms and molecules.
e: Chemical energy is the energy that is stored in the bonds of chemical compounds such as atoms and molecules. Bonds is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Humans release this chemical energy during ____ and use it to power systems inside the body.
e: Humans release this chemical energy during digestion and use it to power systems inside the body. Digestion is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Plants store chemical energy in ____ formed during photosynthesis.
e: Plants store chemical energy in carbohydrates formed during photosynthesis. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: A chemical reaction involves the breaking of bonds in the reactants and the forming of bonds in the ____.
e: A chemical reaction involves the breaking of bonds in the reactants and the forming of bonds in the products. Products appear on the right of the equation and in the numerator of K.

q: Some reactions take place on their own under a given set of conditions, and some are needed to provide ____ for the reaction to proceed.
e: Some reactions take place on their own under a given set of conditions, and some are needed to provide energy for the reaction to proceed. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: A process that can take place on its own accord is called ____.
e: A process that can take place on its own accord is called spontaneous. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: ____ processes need the energy to take place.
e: Non-spontaneous processes need the energy to take place. Non-spontaneous: a spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: Adding a solution of dilute sulphuric acid to a solution of sodium hydroxide is an example of a ____ reaction because the reaction takes place without any energy being added.
e: Adding a solution of dilute sulphuric acid to a solution of sodium hydroxide is an example of a spontaneous reaction because the reaction takes place without any energy being added. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: The reaction between magnesium and oxygen, and the reaction between copper and oxygen are both ____ reactions.
e: The reaction between magnesium and oxygen, and the reaction between copper and oxygen are both non-spontaneous reactions. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: Iron rusting is exothermic and ____.
e: Iron rusting is exothermic and spontaneous. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: When the ice melts at room temperature, that is a spontaneous and ____ process.
e: When the ice melts at room temperature, that is a spontaneous and endothermic process. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: When sulphuric acid is slowly poured into water, the flask or beaker becomes ____.
e: When sulphuric acid is slowly poured into water, the flask or beaker becomes hot. Hot is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Examples of exothermic reactions are burning candle, the combustion of a fuel, the neutralisation reaction, respiration, and ____ of iron.
e: Examples of exothermic reactions are burning candle, the combustion of a fuel, the neutralisation reaction, respiration, and rusting of iron. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: Exothermic reactions give out ____.
e: Exothermic reactions give out energy. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: In exothermic reactions, the energy of the product is ____ than the energy of the reactants because energy has been released during the reaction.
e: In exothermic reactions, the energy of the product is lower than the energy of the reactants because energy has been released during the reaction. Aufbau fills lower-energy orbitals before higher-energy ones.

q: When ammonium chloride is dissolved in water, the flask becomes quite ____ to the touch.
e: When ammonium chloride is dissolved in water, the flask becomes quite cold to the touch. Cold is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Examples of endothermic reactions are melting of ice, cooking an egg, evaporating liquid water, and thermal decomposition of ____.
e: Examples of endothermic reactions are melting of ice, cooking an egg, evaporating liquid water, and thermal decomposition of limestone. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: Endothermic reactions take in energy from the ____.
e: Endothermic reactions take in energy from the surroundings. The surroundings are everything outside the reaction you chose to study.

q: In endothermic reactions, the energy of the products is ____ than the energy of the reactants because energy has been absorbed during the reaction.
e: In endothermic reactions, the energy of the products is higher than the energy of the reactants because energy has been absorbed during the reaction. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: Energy changes in chemical reactions are caused by the making and ____ of chemical bonds.
e: Energy changes in chemical reactions are caused by the making and breaking of chemical bonds. Breaking is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: In a chemical reaction, bonds in the ____ must be broken first.
e: In a chemical reaction, bonds in the reactants must be broken first. Reactants appear on the left and in the denominator of K.

q: Energy is ____ to break bonds.
e: Energy is absorbed to break bonds. Absorbed is the chemical word that makes this relationship true.

q: Bond breaking is an ____ process.
e: Bond breaking is an endothermic process. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.

q: Energy is ____ when new bonds form.
e: Energy is released when new bonds form. Energy is released when a gaseous atom gains an electron.

q: Bond making is an ____ process.
e: Bond making is an exothermic process. The system loses heat, so delta H is negative.

q: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is less than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is ____.
e: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is less than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is exothermic. The system loses heat, so delta H is negative.

q: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is more than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is ____.
e: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is more than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is endothermic. The system gains heat, so delta H is positive.
